You can have a good life and still want more from it.

Maybe you're navigating a transition or reconsidering what matters most. Maybe you're balancing so many responsibilities that your own aspirations keep slipping down the list. Perhaps you've accomplished things you're proud of, but they haven't brought quite the satisfaction you expected.
Or maybe life is going well, and you simply want to be more intentional about enjoying it.

You don't have to be unhappy or facing a crisis to want something more from life. You might want greater clarity, stronger relationships, healthier habits, a stronger sense of purpose, or simply more time and space for the things that bring you joy.
Whatever brings you here, I believe you deserve to be as intentional about the quality of your life as you are about the things you accomplish within it.
Create the life you want. Enjoy the life you have.

We spend a great deal of energy trying to improve our circumstances: our careers, relationships, health, habits, finances, and opportunities. Those things matter. But how we experience our lives is also shaped by what happens within us: our expectations, the stories we tell ourselves, how we respond to challenges, and how kindly we treat ourselves along the way.
Sometimes fulfillment requires changing something about our circumstances. Sometimes it requires changing how we see or experience the lives we're already living. Often, it's both.
I believe we can be ambitious without demanding perfection. Accountable without being cruel to ourselves. Grateful for what we have while still pursuing what we want.
We can learn to navigate challenges, make intentional choices, strengthen our relationships, and create space for experiences that make life meaningful.
And we can do all of that without turning the pursuit of a good life into another source of pressure.
Love your life for what it is, and forgive it for what it isn't.
A thoughtful place to begin.
There is no single formula for a fulfilling life. What brings one person joy, meaning, and satisfaction may look completely different for someone else.
My approach begins with understanding you: your values, experiences, aspirations, challenges, and the things that make you feel most alive.

I bring curiosity, perspective, practical problem-solving, and a willingness to ask questions that help you see things differently. Together, we can explore what's working, what isn't, and what is possible.

Meet Lyla.
A diplomat's perspective on living well.

I'm Lyla Bashan. I spent two decades as a U.S. diplomat, working around the world with people from different cultures and backgrounds to navigate complex challenges, build relationships, resolve conflicts, and turn ambitious goals into practical action.

I now want to take those diplomatic skills and help you apply them to your life. Throughout my career I've been fascinated by what makes people thrive. What helps us navigate uncertainty? How do we make decisions that reflect what matters most? How can we pursue meaningful goals without sacrificing our wellbeing along the way?
These aren't just professional questions for me. I've spent much of my own life putting them into practice.

I've made intentional choices to prioritize my relationships, health, family, adventure, meaningful work, and the everyday experiences that bring me joy. I've taken breaks from my career to travel and spend time with family, embraced opportunities to live and work around the world, and navigated unexpected changes that challenged my assumptions about what life would look like.

Today, I feel deeply fulfilled by the life I've created. Not because everything has gone according to plan or because every part of life is perfect, but because I've learned to be intentional about what matters, appreciate what I have, and keep making room for what brings me joy.

I believe many of the skills that help us navigate a complicated world can also help us navigate our own lives: listening carefully, understanding different perspectives, asking thoughtful questions, recognizing possibilities, making intentional choices, and taking meaningful action.
That's what inspired The Diplomat Within.
My role isn't to tell you what your life should look like. It's to help you discover what matters to you, recognize what's possible, and develop your own way forward.
I'm also the author of Global: An Extraordinary Guide for Ordinary Heroes, and I live on Hawaiʻi Island with my family.
Your life. Your priorities. Your way forward.
Working together isn't about following my formula for happiness or becoming someone you think you should be.

A few common questions
Do I need to have a specific problem or goal?
Not at all. You might be navigating a challenge, contemplating a change, or simply wanting to feel more intentional, connected, or fulfilled. We can begin wherever you are.
What is personal advisory?

I think of it as having a thoughtful, experienced partner who helps you explore important questions, see possibilities, clarify priorities, and turn insights into practical steps. It's collaborative, personal, and tailored to your circumstances.
How is this different from therapy?
My work focuses on personal reflection, life choices, aspirations, and practical action. It isn't psychotherapy, mental health treatment, or a substitute for medical or psychological care.
What happens after the Whole-Life Strategy Session?

You'll receive your personalized Whole-Life Action Roadmap, capturing key insights, priorities, and practical next steps. If you'd like continued support, we can explore a longer-term advisory partnership to help you put your plans into practice, navigate challenges, and make meaningful progress toward the life you want.
Can we meet virtually?
Yes. I offer virtual conversations, making it possible to work together wherever you live. In-person meetings on Hawaiʻi Island may also be arranged.
